whyWrongByChoice.E: Transitional epithelium of sinuses can give rise to sinonasal papilloma, not specifically ONB.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Gemcitabine, used in NPC chemotherapy, acts by which of the following mechanisms?

explanation.summary: Gemcitabine is an antimetabolite pyrimidine analog that inhibits DNA synthesis in the S phase of the cell cycle. Adverse effects include myelosuppression, fatigue, nausea, hair loss, and liver enzyme elevation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gemcitabine is an antimetabolite chemotherapy agent, a pyrimidine analog (similar to cytarabine) that inhibits DNA synthesis in the S phase of the cell cycle. It is used with cisplatin for NPC. Adverse effects include myelosuppression, fatigue, nausea/vomiting, hair loss, liver enzyme elevation, and flu-like symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topoisomerase II inhibition is the mechanism of etoposide and doxorubicin, not gemcitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DNA crosslinking is the mechanism of cisplatin and other alkylating agents, not gemcitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microtubule inhibition is the mechanism of vincristine (vinca alkaloids) and paclitaxel (taxanes), not gemcitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tyrosine kinase inhibition is the mechanism of targeted therapies like erlotinib and gefitinib, not gemcitabine.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma has a higher incidence in certain geographic regions. Which of the following areas has the highest incidence?

explanation.summary: NPC has a higher incidence in Southern China, Southeast Asia, North Africa and the Middle East, and the Arctic. These geographic patterns relate to EBV prevalence, dietary habits (preserved/salted foods), and genetic predisposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: The incidence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is highest in Southern China, Southeast Asia, North Africa and the Middle East, and the Arctic. These geographic patterns are related to the combination of EBV prevalence, dietary habits (preserved foods high in nitrosamines), and genetic predisposition in these populations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Northern Europe has relatively low NPC incidence compared to the high-risk areas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: North America (including the US) is a low-risk area for NPC. In the US, there is a bimodal age distribution when it does occur.
whyWrongByChoice.D: South America is not identified as a high-incidence region for NPC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Australia is not a high-incidence region for NPC.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: The 5-year survival rate for olfactory neuroblastoma ranges from 40% to 90%. Which of the following treatment approaches is standard for ONB?

explanation.summary: ONB is treated with surgery combined with adjuvant radiation therapy, chemotherapy (cisplatin + etoposide), or both. Targeted therapies and immunotherapies have not shown significant benefit in ONB.
explanation.whyCorrect: Olfactory neuroblastoma is treated with a combination of surgery and adjuvant radiation therapy, chemotherapy, or both. The most common chemotherapy regimen is cisplatin + etoposide. Targeted therapies and immunotherapies have not shown as much benefit in ONB, although clinical trials are ongoing. The wide survival range (40-90%) reflects the variability in stage at diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Radiation alone is not the standard approach. Surgery is a critical component of ONB treatment, combined with adjuvant therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cisplatin + gemcitabine is the NPC chemotherapy regimen. ONB uses cisplatin + etoposide, and chemotherapy is combined with surgery, not used alone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunotherapy has not shown significant benefit in ONB and is not first-line.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Watchful waiting is not appropriate for an aggressive malignant tumor like ONB.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which of the following upper respiratory malignancies is the most common overall?

explanation.summary: Laryngeal cancer is the most common of the upper respiratory malignancies discussed, accounting for one-third of head and neck cancers, with an annual incidence of 3:100,000.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laryngeal cancer is the most common of the upper respiratory tract malignancies, accounting for a third of head and neck cancers with an annual incidence of 3:100,000. ONB is very rare (0.4 per million), and while NPC is significant in certain geographic areas, laryngeal cancer is more common overall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ONB is very rare (2% of sinonasal tumors, 0.4 per million). It is not the most common upper respiratory malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NPC is significant in certain geographic regions but is not the most common upper respiratory malignancy overall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sinonasal adenocarcinoma is rare and not the most common.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nasal NK/T-cell lymphoma is rare and not the most common upper respiratory malignancy.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Cisplatin is used in chemotherapy regimens for all three upper respiratory malignancies discussed. Which of the following is cisplatin's primary mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibition of DNA synthesis as a nucleotide analog

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cross-linking of DNA strands preventing replication

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of protein synthesis at the ribosome

explanation.summary: Cisplatin is a platinum-based chemotherapy agent that cross-links DNA strands, preventing DNA replication and transcription, ultimately leading to cell death. It is used in ONB (with etoposide), NPC (with gemcitabine), and laryngeal cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cisplatin is a platinum-based alkylating agent that cross-links DNA strands (both intrastrand and interstrand), preventing DNA replication and transcription. This DNA damage triggers apoptosis. Cisplatin is a backbone of chemotherapy for upper respiratory malignancies: combined with etoposide for ONB, gemcitabine for NPC, and used alone or in combinations for laryngeal cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nucleotide analog activity describes gemcitabine, not cisplatin. Cisplatin directly cross-links DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topoisomerase I inhibition is the mechanism of irinotecan and topotecan, not cisplatin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mitotic spindle blockade is the mechanism of vinca alkaloids (vincristine) and taxanes (paclitaxel), not cisplatin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribosomal protein synthesis inhibition is the mechanism of antibiotics (macrolides, aminoglycosides), not cisplatin.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A patient with laryngeal cancer may require total laryngectomy for advanced disease. Which of the following is the most challenging complication of this surgery?

explanation.summary: Voice loss is a challenging complication for patients who require total laryngectomy. Voice retraining may be required. This is less common with organ-sparing (partial laryngectomy) surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Voice loss is the most challenging complication of total laryngectomy. The larynx contains the vocal cords, so its complete removal eliminates the ability to produce voice normally. Voice retraining may be required. This complication drives the preference for organ-sparing surgery (partial laryngectomy) with radiation when feasible for localized tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic sinusitis is not a typical complication of laryngectomy. It is more associated with nasal/sinus pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epistaxis is associated with nasal tumors (ONB, NPC), not laryngectomy complications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anosmia is associated with olfactory nerve damage (ONB extending through cribriform plate), not laryngectomy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Facial nerve paralysis is not a typical complication of laryngectomy. The facial nerve (CN VII) is not in the surgical field.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Olfactory neuroblastoma can rarely present with paraneoplastic syndromes. Which of the following has been reported?

explanation.summary: Rarely, patients with olfactory neuroblastoma can present with paraneoplastic syndromes including SIADH, hypercalcemia, and ectopic ACTH production—similar to other neuroendocrine tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rarely, patients with olfactory neuroblastoma can present with paraneoplastic syndromes, including SIADH, hypercalcemia, and ectopic ACTH production. This is consistent with ONB's classification as a neuroendocrine tumor, which can produce ectopic hormones.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HUS is not a reported paraneoplastic syndrome of ONB. It is associated with E. coli O157:H7 infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TTP is not a typical paraneoplastic syndrome of ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia is not a characteristic paraneoplastic syndrome of ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nephrotic syndrome is not a characteristic paraneoplastic association with ONB.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the gross appearance of olfactory neuroblastoma?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Single pink or brown friable nasal mass

choices.label: E
choices.text: White keratotic plaque on vocal fold

explanation.summary: ONB usually presents grossly as a single pink or brown friable nasal mass within the nasal cavity. The most common symptom is nasal obstruction due to this mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Olfactory neuroblastoma usually presents grossly as a single pink or brown friable nasal mass within the nasal cavity. Nasal obstruction due to the presence of this mass is the most common presenting symptom.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An ulcerated fungating laryngeal mass describes advanced laryngeal cancer, not ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A smooth violet lobulated mass describes juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA), not ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bilateral translucent polyps describes common nasal polyps, which are benign and bilateral.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A white keratotic plaque on the vocal fold describes laryngeal leukoplakia or early SCC, not ONB.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Laryngeal cancer has a higher prevalence in males and in which of the following racial groups in the United States?

explanation.summary: Laryngeal cancer has a higher prevalence in males and in Black patients. The incidence is dropping in the US due to reduced smoking rates.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laryngeal cancer has a higher prevalence in males and in Black patients. Historically, higher smoking rates in these demographic groups contributed to this disparity. The overall incidence in the United States is now dropping, likely due to reduced smoking.

whyWrongByChoice.A: While White patients develop laryngeal cancer, the prevalence is specifically noted to be higher in Black patients.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hispanic patients are not specifically identified as having higher laryngeal cancer prevalence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Asian patients have lower rates of laryngeal cancer in the US. However, Asian populations (Southern China) have higher rates of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Native American patients are not specifically identified as having higher laryngeal cancer prevalence in this context.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Laryngeal cancer is diagnosed using which of the following procedures as the primary diagnostic tool?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fine needle aspiration of the cervical node

explanation.summary: Laryngeal cancer is diagnosed by flexible laryngoscopy, during which the tumor is visualized and biopsied. CT/MRI are then used for staging to assess invasion and metastasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laryngeal cancer is usually diagnosed by flexible laryngoscopy, during which the tumor is directly visualized and biopsied for histologic confirmation. A thorough assessment of the neck and lymph nodes is also performed. After diagnosis, imaging (CT, MRI, PET) is used for staging to determine the extent of invasion and metastasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CT scan is used for staging after diagnosis, not as the primary diagnostic tool. Laryngoscopy with biopsy is needed for tissue diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PET scan is useful for staging, detection, and follow-up but is not the primary diagnostic procedure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FNA of a cervical lymph node may confirm metastatic disease but does not directly diagnose the primary laryngeal tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There are no specific serum tumor markers used for diagnosing laryngeal cancer.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with progressive left-sided nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, and new anosmia. MRI shows a mass extending through the cribriform plate. Biopsy reveals small round blue cells in lobular nests within fibrovascular stroma, with Homer-Wright pseudorosettes. From which tissue does this tumor arise?

explanation.summary: Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from the olfactory epithelium.
explanation.whyCorrect: ONB (esthesioneuroblastoma) is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from olfactory epithelium in the nasal cavity, explaining the anosmia from cribriform plate extension.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Salivary gland tissue gives rise to salivary neoplasms, not ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Respiratory epithelium lines much of the airway but is not the origin of ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Squamous epithelium origin is seen in laryngeal SCC, not ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nasopharyngeal mucosa gives rise to nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with a sinonasal mass is found to have hyponatremia with serum sodium 122 mEq/L, urine osmolality 600 mOsm/kg, and normal volume status. Biopsy of the nasal mass shows small round blue cells with a lobular architecture in a fibrovascular stroma. What is the most likely underlying mechanism for his sodium abnormality?

explanation.summary: ONB can produce paraneoplastic SIADH.
explanation.whyCorrect: Olfactory neuroblastoma rarely produces paraneoplastic syndromes including SIADH (ectopic ADH) causing euvolemic hyponatremia with concentrated urine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal insufficiency is not typical of ONB paraneoplastic syndromes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PTHrP causes hypercalcemia, not hyponatremia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ectopic ACTH causes Cushing syndrome, not this euvolemic hyponatremia pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cerebral salt wasting shows volume depletion, not the euvolemic pattern here.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with nasal obstruction, epistaxis, and right-sided proptosis with diplopia. Biopsy of a nasal mass shows neuroblasts and neurofibrils in lobular nests within a fibrovascular stroma. What is the most likely explanation for her ocular findings?

explanation.summary: ONB can extend into the orbit causing proptosis and diplopia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Orbital extension of olfactory neuroblastoma causes pain, proptosis, diplopia, and excessive tearing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Optic nerve glioma is unrelated to sinonasal small round blue cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Graves ophthalmopathy is autoimmune and unrelated to this biopsy finding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cavernous sinus thrombosis presents with multiple cranial neuropathies and sepsis-like features.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carotid-cavernous fistula causes pulsatile exophthalmos and bruit, not this biopsy finding.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with biopsy-confirmed olfactory neuroblastoma has imaging showing local invasion into the ethmoid sinuses and orbit without distant metastases. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?

explanation.summary: ONB is treated with surgery combined with radiation and/or chemotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The standard treatment for olfactory neuroblastoma is surgical resection combined with adjuvant radiation, chemotherapy, or both.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Radiation alone is inadequate; surgical excision is a cornerstone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immunotherapy has not shown substantial benefit in ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Targeted therapy has not shown substantial benefit in ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation is inappropriate for an aggressive invasive tumor.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A pathologist reviews a biopsy from a sinonasal mass and identifies small round blue cells in a lobular pattern with nests of neuroblasts and neurofibrils embedded in a vascular fibrous stroma. Which additional histologic feature would most strongly support the diagnosis of olfactory neuroblastoma?

explanation.summary: Homer-Wright pseudorosettes are characteristic of neuroblastomas including ONB.
explanation.whyCorrect: Homer-Wright pseudorosettes and Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes are characteristic pathologic features of neuroblastomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Keratin pearls are seen in squamous cell carcinoma (laryngeal cancer).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Psammoma bodies are seen in papillary thyroid cancer and meningiomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reed-Sternberg cells are seen in Hodgkin lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Signet ring cells are characteristic of gastric adenocarcinoma.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 40-year-old man from Southern China presents with headaches, diplopia, right facial numbness, and a neck mass. Nasal endoscopy reveals a nasopharyngeal mass; biopsy shows nests of epithelioid cells lacking keratinization, with prominent nucleoli and infiltrating lymphocytes. Which virus is most strongly associated with this malignancy?

explanation.summary: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is strongly associated with EBV.
explanation.whyCorrect: EBV is a major risk factor for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, particularly the non-keratinizing undifferentiated type seen in endemic regions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HPV is associated with laryngeal and oropharyngeal cancer, not NPC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CMV is not linked to NPC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma, not NPC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HCV is linked to hepatocellular carcinoma, not NPC.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 50-year-old man of Southeast Asian origin reports a lifelong diet high in salted fish and preserved foods. He now presents with nasal obstruction, epistaxis, and a cervical lymph node mass. Which dietary component is thought to contribute to his cancer risk?

explanation.summary: Preserved foods (salted fish) contain nitrosamines linked to NPC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eating preserved foods such as salted fish leads to high levels of nitrosamines, a known risk factor for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aflatoxins are linked to hepatocellular carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PAHs are linked to lung cancer from smoking/pollution.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heterocyclic amines form during cooking meat and are linked more to colon cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acrylamide is formed in fried starchy foods and not specifically tied to NPC.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman has biopsy-confirmed non-keratinizing undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma that has spread to regional lymph nodes. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?

explanation.summary: NPC is treated with radiotherapy and chemotherapy, not surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is uniquely treated with radiation and chemotherapy (cisplatin + gemcitabine); surgery is very specialized and challenging due to anatomic location.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgery is not the primary treatment for NPC because of anatomic complexity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immunotherapy alone is not first-line therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Observation is inappropriate for invasive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stem cell transplant is not used for NPC.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with nasopharyngeal carcinoma begins chemotherapy with cisplatin and gemcitabine. She develops myelosuppression, fatigue, hair loss, and elevated liver enzymes. Which best describes gemcitabine's mechanism of action?

explanation.summary: Gemcitabine is a pyrimidine analog antimetabolite.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gemcitabine is an antimetabolite chemotherapy, a pyrimidine analog similar to cytarabine that inhibits DNA synthesis during the S phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alkylating/cross-linking is the mechanism of cisplatin, not gemcitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topoisomerase II inhibitors include etoposide, not gemcitabine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microtubule stabilizers include paclitaxel.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Folate antagonists include methotrexate.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history presents with 6 months of progressive hoarseness, a tickling cough, and an enlarged left neck lymph node. Laryngoscopy identifies a mass on the vocal cord. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The presentation is classic for laryngeal SCC in a smoker.
explanation.whyCorrect: Persistent hoarseness, cough, and cervical lymphadenopathy in a long-term smoker strongly suggest laryngeal cancer, most commonly squamous cell carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ONB presents with nasal obstruction and anosmia, not hoarseness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NPC typically presents with cranial nerve findings and nasal obstruction, not vocal cord mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is uncommon and not characterized by this scenario.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sinonasal lymphoma would not present with a vocal cord mass.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 70-year-old man is diagnosed with laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Which anatomic subsite accounts for the majority of laryngeal cancers?

explanation.summary: Supraglottic tumors account for two-thirds of laryngeal cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laryngeal cancers are classified as supraglottic (two-thirds of cases), glottic (one-third), or subglottic (1-2%).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glottic tumors account for about one-third, not the majority.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Subglottic tumors represent only 1-2% of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyriform sinus is part of the hypopharynx, not a standard laryngeal subsite category.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Postcricoid is a hypopharyngeal subsite, not a laryngeal subsite category.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 35-year-old non-smoker presents with hoarseness. Laryngoscopy reveals a glottic mass; biopsy shows squamous cell carcinoma. Which viral oncoprotein most likely drives this cancer by inactivating p53?

explanation.summary: HPV E6 inactivates p53.
explanation.whyCorrect: HPV E6 inactivates the tumor suppressor p53, while E7 inactivates pRb; together they drive uncontrolled cell cycle progression leading to laryngeal/oropharyngeal cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: E7 inactivates pRb, not p53.
whyWrongByChoice.B: LMP1 is associated with EBV-driven NPC, not p53 inactivation in laryngeal SCC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: vGPCR is associated with Kaposi sarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HTLV-1 Tax drives adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with laryngeal SCC has a tumor localized to the larynx without nodal spread. Which treatment strategy best preserves vocal function?

explanation.summary: Localized laryngeal cancer is treated with radiation plus limited (organ-sparing) surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: For tumors localized to the larynx, combined radiation and limited surgery (eg, partial laryngectomy) are used to preserve vocal function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Total laryngectomy is reserved for advanced disease and sacrifices voice.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotherapy alone is not the standard for localized disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunotherapy alone is not first-line for localized laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation risks progression of a curable localized cancer.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A pathologist examines a laryngectomy specimen. Which microscopic feature is most characteristic of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Small round blue cells in lobules

explanation.summary: Laryngeal SCC shows keratin pearls, polygonal cells, and pleomorphic nuclei.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laryngeal SCC pathology typically shows polygonal cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, keratin pearls, and pleomorphic nuclei.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Small round blue cells in lobules describe olfactory neuroblastoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Syncytial clusters with lymphocytes describe non-keratinizing NPC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glandular tubules with mucin are features of adenocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spindle cells with herringbone pattern describe fibrosarcoma.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 62-year-old smoker with laryngeal SCC has biopsy-proven spread to cervical lymph nodes. Which is the most likely chemotherapy agent to be added to his regimen?

explanation.summary: Cisplatin is the most common chemotherapy for laryngeal cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: When laryngeal cancer spreads to adjacent neck structures, chemotherapy is added; the most common agent used is cisplatin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gemcitabine is paired with cisplatin for NPC, not laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Etoposide is used with cisplatin for ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methotrexate is not the standard for laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vincristine is not standard for laryngeal cancer.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with unilateral serous otitis media and ear pain. Nasal endoscopy reveals a nasopharyngeal mass. Which anatomic structure is most likely obstructed by the tumor, causing her ear symptoms?

explanation.summary: Nasopharyngeal tumors obstruct the Eustachian tube causing otitis media.
explanation.whyCorrect: Obstruction of the Eustachian tube by a tumor causes ear pain and otitis media, a classic presentation of nasopharyngeal/sinonasal tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: External auditory canal is not obstructed by nasopharyngeal masses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The round window is intracranial and not obstructed by nasopharyngeal masses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The oval window is part of middle ear ossicle transmission, not obstructed externally.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The cochlear aqueduct connects inner ear to subarachnoid space, not nasopharynx.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with biopsy-proven olfactory neuroblastoma will begin chemotherapy. Which combination regimen is most commonly used for this tumor?

explanation.summary: ONB is typically treated with cisplatin + etoposide.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common chemotherapy regimen for olfactory neuroblastoma is cisplatin plus etoposide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cisplatin + gemcitabine is the regimen for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyclophosphamide + doxorubicin is used for lymphomas/breast cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carboplatin + paclitaxel is common in NSCLC and ovarian cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methotrexate + 5-FU is not the standard ONB regimen.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with hoarseness, dysphagia, and odynophagia for several months along with recent weight loss. Which finding most strongly suggests metastatic disease rather than local complications?

explanation.summary: Rapid weight loss suggests metastatic laryngeal cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rapid weight loss is described as a feature of metastatic laryngeal cancer; the other symptoms reflect local disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Persistent cough occurs with localized laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Voice change typically reflects local vocal cord involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Odynophagia reflects local invasion, not metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dysphagia reflects local extension, not metastases.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 50-year-old shipyard worker with a 30-pack-year smoking history presents with hoarseness and is diagnosed with laryngeal SCC. Besides tobacco, which occupational exposure most likely contributed to his cancer?

explanation.summary: Occupational asbestos exposure is a risk factor for laryngeal cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Occupational exposure to asbestos, radiation, paint, and gas fumes are cited risk factors for laryngeal cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Silica is linked primarily to silicosis and lung cancer, not specifically laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coal dust is associated with pneumoconiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beryllium causes berylliosis, not specifically laryngeal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cotton dust causes byssinosis, not laryngeal cancer.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 30-year-old man from North Africa presents with a left neck mass, diplopia, and facial numbness. Endoscopic biopsy shows syncytial clusters of malignant epithelial cells infiltrated by benign lymphocytes, positive for EBV. Which histologic subtype of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is this?

explanation.summary: The non-keratinizing undifferentiated type is most common and EBV-associated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Non-keratinizing undifferentiated NPC (60-65% of cases) shows syncytial clusters of tumor cells with lymphocytic infiltrate and strong EBV association.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Keratinizing type accounts for 20-25% and shows more keratinization.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Basaloid squamous type is rare (1-2%).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Non-keratinizing differentiated type is less common (10-15%).
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adenosquamous is not among the four common NPC subtypes.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with progressive unilateral nasal obstruction and epistaxis. MRI shows a sinonasal mass extending through the cribriform plate into the anterior cranial fossa. Biopsy shows lobular small round blue cells in fibrovascular stroma. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is LEAST likely associated with his tumor?

explanation.summary: ONB is associated with SIADH, hypercalcemia, and ectopic ACTH but not cerebellar degeneration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Olfactory neuroblastoma rarely causes paraneoplastic syndromes including SIADH, hypercalcemia, and ectopic ACTH; paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration is not described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SIADH is a recognized paraneoplastic syndrome of ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic ACTH is a described paraneoplastic syndrome in ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypercalcemia is a described paraneoplastic syndrome in ONB.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyponatremia (from SIADH) is an expected ONB paraneoplastic finding.

questions.topicName: Malignant Tumors of the Upper Respiratory System (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with hoarseness is found to have a supraglottic mass on laryngoscopy, and biopsy confirms SCC. Which is the most common site of metastasis for laryngeal cancer?

explanation.summary: Laryngeal cancer commonly metastasizes to local lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: All laryngeal cancer subsites commonly metastasize to local lymph nodes; distant metastases occur but are less common initially.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lung metastases occur but are less common than local lymph node spread.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Liver is not the most common site of laryngeal cancer metastasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bone metastases occur in late/advanced disease, not most commonly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Brain metastases are uncommon in laryngeal cancer.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: A 68-year-old smoker with a 40-pack-year history presents with confusion and weight loss. Serum sodium is 117 mEq/L. Chest X-ray shows a perihilar lung mass. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism causing his hyponatremia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tumor secretion of ADH causing SIADH

explanation.summary: SCLC commonly secretes ectopic ADH, causing SIADH with increased water reabsorption and hyponatremia. SIADH occurs in ~10% of SCLC patients and is the most common paraneoplastic syndrome in this cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC is derived from neuroendocrine progenitor cells that can secrete ectopic ADH (vasopressin). The resulting SIADH causes increased renal water reabsorption, leading to increased total body water and dilutional hyponatremia. This is the most common paraneoplastic syndrome in SCLC (10% of patients). Confusion from severe hyponatremia (117 mEq/L) is a common presenting symptom.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Renal salt wasting occurs in CNS pathology and Legionella infection, not typically as a paraneoplastic mechanism of SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: While adrenal metastasis can occur in SCLC, the perihilar mass with severe hyponatremia in a heavy smoker points to SIADH from ectopic ADH production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polydipsia would not be the primary cause in the context of a perihilar mass in a heavy smoker. Ectopic ADH from SCLC is much more likely.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no mention of diuretic use. The perihilar mass and smoking history point to tumor-related SIADH.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC is derived from neuroendocrine progenitor cells. Which of the following histologic features is characteristic of SCLC under the microscope?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Large cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm

explanation.summary: SCLC shows small cells with scant cytoplasm, dispersed 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin (finely granular, speckled pattern), and inconspicuous nucleoli—characteristic of neuroendocrine tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under the microscope, SCLC is composed of small cells with scant cytoplasm. At higher power, the malignant cells show dispersed 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin (finely granular, speckled pattern with dark granules interspersed with lighter areas) and inconspicuous nucleoli. This chromatin pattern is characteristic of neuroendocrine tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Large cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm would suggest large cell carcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glandular acini formation is characteristic of adenocarcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratin pearls with intercellular bridges are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clear cells with lipid-rich cytoplasm suggest renal cell carcinoma or certain adrenal tumors, not SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC has the strongest association with tobacco smoking among all lung cancers. Approximately what percentage of SCLC occurs in nonsmokers?

explanation.summary: Only about 1% of SCLC occurs in nonsmokers, making it the lung cancer most strongly associated with smoking. This is compared to ~10% of all lung cancers occurring in nonsmokers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among lung cancers, SCLC has the strongest association with tobacco smoking. Only about 1% of SCLC occurs in nonsmokers, compared to approximately 10% of all lung cancers. Smoking-induced somatic mutations in tumor suppressor genes (TP53, RB) and oncogene amplification (MYC) drive SCLC development.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 10% is the approximate rate of all lung cancers in nonsmokers, not SCLC specifically. SCLC's nonsmoker rate is even lower at ~1%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 25% significantly overestimates nonsmoker SCLC cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 40% would mean nearly half of SCLC occurs without smoking, which is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 50% would mean equal rates in smokers and nonsmokers, which is far from reality for SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: The Azzopardi effect is a histologic finding in SCLC. Which of the following best describes this phenomenon?

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNA encrustation of blood vessel walls

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keratin pearl formation in necrotic areas

choices.label: E
choices.text: Palisading of nuclei at the tumor periphery

explanation.summary: The Azzopardi effect occurs when rapidly growing SCLC outgrows its blood supply, causing central necrosis. Released cellular debris including DNA adheres to and 'incrusts' nearby blood vessel walls, visible as basophilic deposits.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC tumors are high grade with rapid growth that often outstrips their blood supply, causing central necrosis. Released cellular debris, including DNA, adheres to and 'incrusts' the walls of nearby blood vessels, visible histologically as basophilic granular deposits. This is the Azzopardi effect, seen in SCLC and other high-grade neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glandular differentiation is a feature of adenocarcinoma, not SCLC. SCLC shows neuroendocrine differentiation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Keratin pearl formation is characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rosette formation (Homer-Wright pseudorosettes) is seen in olfactory neuroblastoma and other neuroblastic tumors, not specifically the Azzopardi effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nuclear palisading is seen in schwannomas and some other tumors, not the Azzopardi effect of SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: The most common chemotherapy regimen for SCLC is cisplatin combined with which of the following agents?

explanation.summary: The most common chemotherapy regimen for SCLC is cisplatin + etoposide. Etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor that prevents religation of DNA double-strand breaks during the S/early G2 phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: The standard chemotherapy regimen for SCLC is cisplatin + etoposide. Cisplatin cross-links DNA, and etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor that inhibits religation of double-strand breaks during the S or early G2 phase of the cell cycle. Adverse effects of etoposide include myelosuppression, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and diarrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cisplatin + gemcitabine is the regimen for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paclitaxel may be used in some lung cancer regimens but cisplatin + etoposide is the standard for SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxorubicin is used in other cancers (breast, lymphoma) but is not the standard SCLC combination with cisplatin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methotrexate is an antimetabolite used in other cancers but is not part of standard SCLC chemotherapy.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC tumor cells express neuroendocrine markers on immunohistochemistry. Which of the following markers confirm neuroendocrine differentiation?

explanation.summary: SCLC tumor cells express neuroendocrine markers including chromogranin and synaptophysin, confirming their origin from neuroendocrine progenitor cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because SCLC is derived from neuroendocrine progenitor cells, tumor cells often express neuroendocrine markers such as chromogranin (a secretory granule protein) and synaptophysin (a synaptic vesicle protein). These immunohistochemical markers help confirm the neuroendocrine differentiation and distinguish SCLC from other lung cancer types.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytokeratin 5/6 and p63 are markers of squamous cell differentiation, not neuroendocrine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TTF-1 and napsin A are markers of lung adenocarcinoma, not specifically neuroendocrine differentiation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD20 and CD79a are B cell markers used in lymphoma diagnosis, not lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S-100 and HMB-45 are melanoma markers, not neuroendocrine markers.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Approximately 70% of SCLC patients present with overt metastatic disease. Which of the following is the most common site of SCLC metastasis?

explanation.summary: SCLC frequently metastasizes to lymph nodes, brain/spinal cord, liver, bone, bone marrow, adrenal glands, and skin. ~70% of patients present with metastatic disease at diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC has a particular propensity to spread widely. The most common metastatic sites include lymph nodes, brain/spinal cord, liver, bone, bone marrow, adrenal glands, and skin. Approximately 70% of patients present with overt metastatic disease at diagnosis, explaining why surgery is rarely beneficial.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skin can be a metastatic site for SCLC, but metastasis occurs at multiple sites simultaneously, not skin only.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kidneys are not the most common exclusive metastatic site. SCLC spreads to multiple organs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spleen and thymus are not the primary metastatic sites for SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GI tract alone is not the predominant metastatic pattern. SCLC metastasizes to liver, brain, bone, and adrenals preferentially.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC most commonly appears on imaging as which of the following?

explanation.summary: SCLC most commonly shows a central (perihilar) mass on imaging, similar to squamous cell carcinoma. Because of its central location, bronchoscopy is the preferred biopsy method.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC most commonly presents as a central (perihilar) mass on imaging. This central location is important for diagnosis because it makes bronchoscopy the preferred method for biopsy, as transthoracic needle biopsy risks damaging adjacent mediastinal structures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peripheral coin lesions are more characteristic of adenocarcinoma. SCLC is centrally located.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bilateral ground-glass opacities are more characteristic of viral pneumonia or PCP, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cavitary upper lobe lesions are more associated with reactivation TB, squamous cell carcinoma, or Nocardia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcified mediastinal lymph nodes suggest prior granulomatous disease (TB, histoplasmosis), not SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome occurs in approximately 3% of SCLC patients. The muscle weakness in this syndrome is caused by autoantibodies against which of the following targets?

explanation.summary: Lambert-Eaton syndrome is caused by autoantibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels at the neuromuscular junction, reducing acetylcholine release and causing proximal muscle weakness.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome is caused by autoantibodies produced by the tumor that target presynaptic calcium channels on neurons at the neuromuscular junction. This reduces calcium-dependent acetylcholine release, leading to proximal muscle weakness (particularly lower extremities), fatigue, diaphragmatic weakness, and bulbar symptoms. It occurs in about 3% of SCLC patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoantibodies against postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors cause myasthenia gravis (MG), not Lambert-Eaton. MG is associated with thymoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (drugs like pyridostigmine) treat MG. Autoantibodies against the enzyme are not the mechanism of Lambert-Eaton.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MuSK antibodies cause a variant of myasthenia gravis, not Lambert-Eaton syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Voltage-gated sodium channel antibodies are not the target in Lambert-Eaton. Calcium channels are the target.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC has mutations in tumor suppressor genes TP53 and RB. Additionally, which of the following oncogenes is often amplified in SCLC?

explanation.summary: The MYC gene family (C-MYC, N-MYC, L-MYC) is often amplified in SCLC, driving tumor cell proliferation. Some tumors also overexpress BCL2, suppressing apoptosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In SCLC, tumor suppressor genes TP53 and RB are commonly nonfunctional/dysfunctional. Additionally, the MYC gene is often amplified, driving tumor cell proliferation. Some SCLC tumors also overexpress BCL2 (an anti-apoptotic protein), further suppressing programmed cell death and allowing cancerous cells to survive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EGFR mutations are associated with adenocarcinoma (NSCLC), not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ALK rearrangements are associated with adenocarcinoma (NSCLC), not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BRAF mutations are associated with adenocarcinoma (NSCLC) and melanoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HER2 amplification is associated with breast cancer and some gastric cancers, not typically SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Most patients with SCLC are not surgical candidates. Which of the following best explains why surgery is rarely an option?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The tumor is too small to locate surgically

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most patients present with metastatic disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: SCLC only occurs in patients too elderly for surgery

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tumor is always located in the pleural space

explanation.summary: Approximately 70% of SCLC patients present with metastatic disease at diagnosis. With widespread disease, surgical resection of the primary tumor would not be curative, so chemotherapy and radiation are the mainstays of treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC patients often have metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis (~70%), making surgical resection unlikely to be beneficial. Only patients with a single lung mass and no metastatic spread can undergo surgery with postoperative chemotherapy, but this is uncommon. Chemotherapy with or without radiation is the main treatment for most SCLC patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SCLC typically presents as a visible central mass, not a tumor too small to find.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no issue with SCLC and anesthesia. The problem is metastatic disease making surgery non-curative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: While SCLC typically presents in older adults (smokers), age alone is not the primary reason surgery is avoided. Metastatic disease is the key factor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC is centrally located (perihilar), not in the pleural space.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: The median survival for SCLC with limited disease (cancer in one lung or nearby lymph nodes) is approximately which of the following?

explanation.summary: Median survival for limited SCLC is 15-20 months with treatment. For extensive disease (metastatic), median survival is 8-13 months. SCLC has the poorest prognosis among lung cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Due to SCLC's aggressive nature, median survival is 15-20 months for limited disease (cancer in one lung or nearby lymph nodes) and 8-13 months for extensive disease (cancer in the other lung or metastasis to distant organs). Despite initial response to chemotherapy, recurrence is common and prognosis remains poor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 3-5 months would be even worse than the already poor prognosis. Limited SCLC median survival is 15-20 months.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 8-13 months is the median survival for extensive (widely metastatic) SCLC, not limited disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 3-5 years is too optimistic for SCLC. Even limited disease has median survival of only 15-20 months.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 10+ years greatly overestimates SCLC survival.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Bronchial carcinoid tumors differ from SCLC in that carcinoids are which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exclusively found in the peripheral lung

explanation.summary: Bronchial carcinoids are low-grade, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, in contrast to SCLC which is high-grade and poorly differentiated. Both express neuroendocrine markers and have neuroendocrine morphology.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bronchial carcinoid tumors are low-grade/well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, in contrast to SCLC which is high-grade/poorly differentiated. Carcinoids are typically located in central airways and cause airway obstruction symptoms. Like SCLC, they express neuroendocrine markers and show neuroendocrine morphology, but their clinical behavior is far less aggressive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: High-grade and poorly differentiated describes SCLC, not carcinoid tumors. Carcinoids are low-grade.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both carcinoids and SCLC are neuroendocrine tumors, not squamous-derived.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Carcinoids are typically central (in central airways), not peripheral.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carcinoids are not specifically associated with asbestos. SCLC is associated with smoking.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Etoposide, part of the standard SCLC regimen, exerts its anticancer effect by inhibiting which of the following enzymes?

explanation.summary: Etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor. It prevents religation of double-strand DNA breaks during the S/early G2 phase, leading to DNA damage and cell death.
explanation.whyCorrect: Etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor that prevents the religation of double-strand DNA breaks created by the enzyme during the S phase or early G2 phase of the cell cycle. This leads to accumulation of DNA damage and ultimately cell death. Adverse effects include myelosuppression, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and diarrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topoisomerase I inhibition is the mechanism of irinotecan and topotecan, not etoposide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA gyrase is the target of fluoroquinolones in bacteria. Etoposide targets human topoisomerase II in cancer cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RNA polymerase inhibition is the mechanism of rifampin (antibacterial), not etoposide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymidylate synthase inhibition is the mechanism of 5-fluorouracil, not etoposide.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: A patient with SCLC and severe, symptomatic hyponatremia (Na 110 mEq/L) presents with seizures. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment for the hyponatremia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chemotherapy to treat the underlying tumor

explanation.summary: Severe, symptomatic hyponatremia with seizures requires emergency treatment with hypertonic saline. While chemotherapy will address the underlying SIADH over weeks, acute symptomatic hyponatremia is life-threatening.
explanation.whyCorrect: Severe, symptomatic hyponatremia (seizures, confusion) requires immediate treatment with hypertonic saline to raise serum sodium and prevent neurological damage. While chemotherapy will ultimately address the underlying SIADH by treating the tumor (hyponatremia usually resolves within several weeks of starting chemo), acute treatment of life-threatening hyponatremia takes priority.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemotherapy addresses the underlying cause (tumor-secreted ADH) but takes weeks to reduce sodium. Acute seizures from hyponatremia require immediate correction with hypertonic saline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluid restriction is used for mild, chronic SIADH but is insufficient for acute symptomatic hyponatremia with seizures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ADH receptor agonists would worsen SIADH by enhancing ADH effects. ADH receptor antagonists (vaptans) could be considered but hypertonic saline is standard for acute emergencies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Isotonic normal saline alone may not adequately correct severe hyponatremia quickly enough in the setting of seizures.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Cushing syndrome as a paraneoplastic manifestation of SCLC is caused by ectopic secretion of which of the following hormones?

explanation.summary: Ectopic ACTH secretion by SCLC (1-5% of patients) stimulates the adrenal glands to produce excess cortisol, causing Cushing syndrome with weight gain, muscle weakness, thin skin, and truncal obesity.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC can secrete ectopic ACTH (1-5% of patients), which stimulates the adrenal glands to produce excess cortisol. This causes Cushing syndrome with weight gain, muscle weakness, thin and fragile skin, truncal obesity, and other cushingoid features. This is less common than SIADH (10%) but is an important paraneoplastic syndrome to recognize.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ADH secretion causes SIADH and hyponatremia, not Cushing syndrome. ADH is the most common paraneoplastic hormone in SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PTHrP causes hypercalcemia and is most associated with squamous cell carcinoma, not Cushing syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Growth hormone excess causes acromegaly, not Cushing syndrome. Ectopic GH is not a common SCLC paraneoplastic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TSH secretion by tumors is extremely rare and is not a recognized SCLC paraneoplastic syndrome.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC is best biopsied by bronchoscopy rather than transthoracic needle biopsy. Which of the following best explains this preference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: SCLC cells are too small for needle biopsy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Central tumor location makes needle biopsy riskier

choices.label: E
choices.text: SCLC only grows within the bronchial lumen

explanation.summary: SCLC is centrally oriented in the thorax (perihilar mass). Transthoracic needle biopsy risks damaging adjacent mediastinal structures. Bronchoscopy allows safer access to the centrally located tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because most SCLC is centrally oriented in the thorax (perihilar location), bronchoscopy provides safer access to the tumor for biopsy. Transthoracic needle biopsy carries risk of damaging adjacent mediastinal structures when targeting a central mass.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cell size is not the issue. Needle biopsies can sample small cells. The concern is the central location of the tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tissue sample size is not the primary reason. Safety considerations due to the tumor's central location drive the preference.
whyWrongByChoice.D: While tumor seeding is a theoretical concern, the primary reason for avoiding transthoracic needle biopsy is the risk of mediastinal injury with centrally located tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC does not only grow within the bronchial lumen. It forms a mass that invades surrounding tissue, but is centrally located.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC overexpression of BCL2 contributes to tumor survival by which of the following mechanisms?

explanation.summary: BCL2 is an anti-apoptotic protein. Its overexpression in SCLC suppresses programmed cell death (apoptosis), allowing cancerous cells to survive despite accumulating DNA damage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some SCLC tumors overexpress BCL2, an anti-apoptotic protein. BCL2 suppresses programmed cell death (apoptosis), allowing cancerous cells to survive despite DNA damage. Combined with loss of tumor suppressors (TP53, RB) and MYC amplification, BCL2 overexpression contributes to the aggressive behavior of SCLC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCL2 does not promote DNA repair. It prevents apoptosis, allowing cells with damaged DNA to survive.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BCL2 does not directly increase angiogenesis. Other factors (VEGF) drive new blood vessel formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BCL2's mechanism is anti-apoptotic, not immune evasion. Immune checkpoint molecules (PD-L1) are involved in immune evasion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: BCL2 does not activate cell cycle checkpoints. TP53 and RB are the checkpoint regulators. BCL2 prevents the death of cells that bypass these checkpoints.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: Immunotherapy agents atezolizumab and pembrolizumab may be added to chemotherapy for SCLC. These agents target which of the following immune checkpoint pathways?

explanation.summary: Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1) and pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) block the PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint pathway, allowing T cells to attack tumor cells that express PD-L1 to evade immune detection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Atezolizumab and pembrolizumab are immune checkpoint inhibitors that target the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway. Atezolizumab blocks PD-L1 on tumor cells, while pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 on T cells. By blocking this checkpoint, T cells are reactivated to attack tumor cells. These agents may be added to cisplatin/etoposide chemotherapy for SCLC based on genetic testing results.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CTLA-4 pathway is targeted by ipilimumab, not atezolizumab or pembrolizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD28/B7 costimulation is a T cell activation pathway, not the target of these checkpoint inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IL-2 receptor pathway is targeted by different immunotherapies (basiliximab, aldesleukin), not PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TNF-α signaling is targeted by anti-TNF biologics (infliximab, adalimumab) for autoimmune diseases, not cancer immunotherapy.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: All SCLC tumors are considered which of the following grades?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Benign with potential for malignant transformation

explanation.summary: All SCLC tumors are high grade with a high mitotic rate and rapid growth. They often outgrow their blood supply, leading to central necrosis (Azzopardi effect). This aggressive behavior explains the poor prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: All small cell lung tumors are high grade, with a high mitotic rate and rapid growth. They frequently outgrow their blood supply, causing central necrosis. This aggressive biology explains why SCLC is the most aggressive lung cancer type, often metastatic at diagnosis, with median survival of only 8-20 months.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SCLC is never low grade. Bronchial carcinoids are the low-grade neuroendocrine tumors. SCLC is always high grade.
whyWrongByChoice.B: SCLC is not intermediate grade. It is uniformly high grade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: All SCLC is high grade regardless of stage. Grade and stage are different concepts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC is always malignant. Benign neuroendocrine tumors of the lung are carcinoids, not SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: SCLC is thought to originate from which of the following cell types in the bronchial wall?

explanation.summary: SCLC originates from bronchial neuroendocrine cells, which are normal constituents of the airway that secrete various amines and polypeptide hormones. This origin explains the neuroendocrine markers and paraneoplastic hormone secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC is thought to originate from bronchial neuroendocrine cells, which are normal constituents of the airway that secrete various amines and polypeptide hormones like DOPA. This neuroendocrine origin explains why SCLC cells express neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin, synaptophysin) and can secrete ectopic hormones (ADH, ACTH) causing paraneoplastic syndromes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ciliated columnar epithelial cells are the predominant cell type in the respiratory epithelium but do not give rise to SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Goblet cells produce mucus and do not give rise to SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type II pneumocytes produce surfactant and are the cell of origin for some adenocarcinomas, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Basal stem cells can give rise to squamous cell carcinoma (through squamous metaplasia), not specifically SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer
questions.stem: When the cancer is limited (confined to one lung and nearby lymph nodes), SCLC is treated with chemotherapy combined with radiation, with the goal of which of the following?

explanation.summary: For limited SCLC, chemotherapy and radiation together are used as initial therapy with the goal of curing the cancer. For extensive disease, chemotherapy alone is used to slow growth, reduce symptoms, and improve survival (not curative).
explanation.whyCorrect: For limited SCLC (cancer in only one lung or nearby lymph nodes), chemotherapy and radiation therapy can be used together as initial therapy with the goal of curing the cancer. However, for extensive (widespread) disease, chemotherapy is used alone to slow cancer growth, reduce symptoms, and improve survival, without the expectation of cure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: In limited disease, the treatment goal is curative, not purely palliative. Palliation is the goal for extensive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The combined chemo-radiation approach is used to cure the cancer, not to prevent surgical complications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: While paraneoplastic symptoms do improve with treatment, the primary goal for limited disease is cancer cure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Most SCLC patients do not undergo surgery. The chemo-radiation regimen is the definitive treatment for limited disease, not preparation for surgery.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history is brought in by his daughter for worsening confusion over the past month. He has lost 15 lb. He is oriented only to place. Labs reveal serum sodium of 117 mEq/L. Chest x-ray shows a perihilar mass. Head CT is normal. Which mechanism best explains his hyponatremia?

explanation.summary: SIADH from SCLC causes euvolemic hyponatremia.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC cells ectopically secrete ADH (SIADH), causing water retention and dilutional hyponatremia; seen in ~10% of SCLC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACTH causes Cushing syndrome, not hyponatremia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Head CT is normal; no intracranial pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adrenal metastases cause hyperkalemia and volume depletion, not SIADH pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP causes hypercalcemia (squamous cell), not hyponatremia.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 62-year-old smoker is diagnosed with SCLC. Biopsy shows small cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin with interspersed lighter areas, and inconspicuous nucleoli. This characteristic chromatin pattern is most specifically associated with which cell lineage?

explanation.summary: Salt-and-pepper chromatin is a hallmark of neuroendocrine tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC arises from bronchial neuroendocrine cells; salt-and-pepper chromatin is characteristic of neuroendocrine neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Squamous cancers show keratin pearls and intercellular bridges.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adenocarcinoma shows glandular/mucinous features.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesothelioma has distinct papillary architecture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphoid cells lack this chromatin pattern.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with SCLC develops truncal obesity, purple striae, and proximal muscle weakness. Labs show hypokalemia and hyperglycemia. Which ectopic hormone best explains these findings?

explanation.summary: Ectopic ACTH causes paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome in SCLC.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC secretes ACTH in 1-5% of patients, causing Cushing syndrome with weight gain, muscle weakness, thin/fragile skin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ADH causes SIADH/hyponatremia, not Cushing features.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PTHrP is associated with squamous cell lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Calcitonin is associated with medullary thyroid cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serotonin relates to carcinoid syndrome.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 65-year-old smoker with SCLC complains of proximal muscle weakness that improves with repeated exertion. Which autoantibody is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: LEMS in SCLC is mediated by antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome involves antibodies to presynaptic calcium channels, causing decreased ACh release; strength improves with repeated use.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-AChR causes myasthenia gravis (worsens with use).
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti-MuSK is another myasthenia gravis variant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-Hu causes paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anti-Yo causes cerebellar degeneration.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 67-year-old man is diagnosed with extensive-stage SCLC. Which initial treatment approach is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: Extensive-stage SCLC is treated primarily with systemic chemotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cisplatin + etoposide is the standard first-line regimen for SCLC, used alone in extensive disease to slow growth and improve survival.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgery is almost never appropriate; most patients have metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation alone is insufficient for widespread disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: EGFR inhibitors are used in NSCLC, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC is too aggressive to observe.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A pathologist examining an SCLC biopsy notes basophilic DNA deposits encrusting small blood vessel walls adjacent to areas of tumor necrosis. What is this finding called?

explanation.summary: The Azzopardi effect reflects DNA encrustation of vessel walls in high-grade tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: In SCLC, necrotic tumor cells release DNA that adheres to blood vessel walls, producing basophilic encrustation known as the Azzopardi effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crush artifact distorts cells mechanically; not vessel encrustation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Psammoma bodies are laminated calcifications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Schiller-Duval bodies occur in yolk sac tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Call-Exner bodies occur in granulosa cell tumors.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 64-year-old smoker is found to have a centrally located lung mass. To definitively diagnose suspected SCLC while minimizing risk to mediastinal structures, which procedure is preferred?

explanation.summary: Central SCLC masses are best biopsied bronchoscopically.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC is typically central; bronchoscopy accesses it safely. Transthoracic needle biopsy risks damaging mediastinal structures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Transthoracic needle biopsy risks injury to central mediastinal vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Open surgery is not first-line for diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sputum cytology is insensitive for definitive diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Most patients lack diagnostic pleural effusion.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with SCLC is started on chemotherapy. His sodium is 118 mEq/L and he is acutely confused with a seizure. What is the most appropriate immediate intervention?

explanation.summary: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia requires hypertonic saline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptomatic severe hyponatremia (confusion, seizures) requires hypertonic saline to rapidly but carefully raise serum sodium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fluid restriction is too slow for seizures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isotonic saline may worsen SIADH-related hyponatremia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loop diuretic alone is inadequate monotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chemo effect takes weeks; patient needs immediate intervention.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: An SCLC tumor shows gene amplification driving uncontrolled proliferation. Which oncogene is most commonly amplified in SCLC?

explanation.summary: MYC is commonly amplified in SCLC.
explanation.whyCorrect: MYC amplification drives tumor cell proliferation in SCLC.

whyWrongByChoice.B: EGFR mutations characterize adenocarcinoma of the lung.
whyWrongByChoice.C: KRAS is common in NSCLC adenocarcinoma, not SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HER2 is relevant to breast/gastric cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: ALK rearrangements occur in NSCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 69-year-old smoker with SCLC has immunohistochemistry performed on biopsy tissue. Which pair of markers most strongly supports the neuroendocrine origin?

explanation.summary: Chromogranin and synaptophysin are classic neuroendocrine markers.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC tumor cells express chromogranin and synaptophysin, confirming neuroendocrine differentiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CK7/TTF-1 are nonspecific lung epithelial markers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: p40 and CK5/6 indicate squamous differentiation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Calretinin/WT-1 mark mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD20/CD79a mark B-cell lymphoma.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 66-year-old man is newly diagnosed with SCLC confined to one hemithorax and regional lymph nodes without distant metastasis. What is the expected median survival with treatment?

explanation.summary: Limited-stage SCLC has 15-20 month median survival.
explanation.whyCorrect: Limited-stage disease (one lung plus nearby nodes) has median survival of 15-20 months with chemoradiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Too short; applies to untreated late disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Too short for limited stage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 8-13 months is expected for extensive-stage disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC rarely has such long survival; mortality is high.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with SCLC is started on a chemotherapy agent that inhibits religation of double-strand DNA breaks during S/early G2 phase. Which drug is this?

explanation.summary: Etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II religation of double-strand DNA breaks during S/early G2 phases, core to SCLC therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cisplatin cross-links DNA; it does not inhibit topoisomerase II.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paclitaxel stabilizes microtubules.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxorubicin intercalates DNA and generates free radicals.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 65-year-old patient with SCLC on cisplatin-etoposide develops fatigue, pallor, easy bruising, and fevers. CBC shows pancytopenia. Which drug effect best explains this?

explanation.summary: Etoposide causes myelosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Etoposide commonly causes myelosuppression, producing pancytopenia with fatigue, bruising, and infection risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nephrotoxicity is a cisplatin effect but doesn't cause pancytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ototoxicity is a cisplatin effect unrelated to CBC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuropathy is a cisplatin effect, not marrow related.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cardiotoxicity is characteristic of doxorubicin.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with SCLC has lesions on imaging raising concern for metastasis. Which combination represents the most common metastatic sites for SCLC?

explanation.summary: SCLC preferentially metastasizes to liver, adrenals, bone, marrow, and brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC has propensity for liver, adrenals, bone, bone marrow, and brain; ~70% present with overt metastases.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These are uncommon SCLC metastatic sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin is possible but thyroid/larynx aren't typical.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Not typical distribution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Not characteristic sites.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman presents with a central bronchial neuroendocrine tumor causing wheezing and recurrent pneumonia. Biopsy shows well-differentiated cells with rosettes and trabecular patterns. This tumor is best classified as:

explanation.summary: Bronchial carcinoids are low-grade, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bronchial carcinoids are well-differentiated, central neuroendocrine tumors causing obstructive symptoms, with rosette/trabecular patterns.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SCLC is poorly differentiated/high-grade, not trabecular/rosetted.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Squamous cell shows keratinization and pearls.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adenocarcinoma shows glandular patterns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mesothelioma arises from pleura.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A molecular pathologist reviews the genetic profile of an SCLC tumor. Which pair of tumor suppressor genes is most commonly mutated?

explanation.summary: TP53 and RB are hallmark mutations in SCLC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Smoking-induced somatic mutations in TP53 and RB are commonly found in SCLC, enabling uncontrolled division and reduced apoptosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: APC/BRCA1 are colorectal/breast-related.
whyWrongByChoice.C: VHL/NF1 relate to renal/neurofibromatosis syndromes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: WT1/PTEN not characteristic of SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MLH1/MSH2 cause Lynch syndrome.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with SCLC-related SIADH is hyponatremic. After two weeks of chemotherapy, sodium normalizes. What is the underlying reason for resolution?

explanation.summary: Tumor cytoreduction reduces ectopic ADH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: As chemotherapy reduces tumor burden, ectopic ADH production falls, resolving SIADH-related hyponatremia over several weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemo does not directly stimulate V2 receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chemo does not cause DI.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Steroids aren't the mechanism of SIADH resolution here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Renal perfusion isn't the primary issue.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 60-year-old former smoker has a solitary peripheral lung nodule without evidence of nodal or distant spread; biopsy reveals SCLC. Which treatment approach is most appropriate in this uncommon scenario?

explanation.summary: Isolated SCLC without metastasis may be resected with adjuvant chemo.
explanation.whyCorrect: A single lung mass without metastatic spread can rarely undergo surgical resection followed by postoperative chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SCLC is too aggressive to observe.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Monotherapy immunotherapy isn't standard first line for localized SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Palliative radiation is inadequate for potentially curable disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormonal therapy has no role in SCLC.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: SCLC represents approximately what percentage of all primary lung cancers?

explanation.summary: SCLC accounts for about 15% of primary lung cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: SCLC represents roughly 15% of all primary lung cancers but is the most aggressive subtype.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Too low; 1% represents SCLC in nonsmokers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Too low.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adenocarcinoma is closer to this proportion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Far too high.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 70-year-old with SCLC receives chemotherapy and is also considered for adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor. Which agent is most commonly added in this setting?

explanation.summary: Atezolizumab (or pembrolizumab) is added as adjuvant immunotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with SCLC may benefit from atezolizumab or pembrolizumab as adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors alongside chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rituximab targets CD20 for B-cell lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Trastuzumab is for HER2 breast/gastric cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cetuximab is anti-EGFR used in colon/head-neck.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bevacizumab is anti-VEGF for other lung cancers.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman presents with fatigue and hemoptysis. She is diagnosed with extensive-stage SCLC, with hyponatremia due to SIADH. Her mental status is normal. Which approach best addresses her hyponatremia?

explanation.summary: In asymptomatic SCLC-SIADH, treating the tumor with chemotherapy resolves hyponatremia.
explanation.whyCorrect: In asymptomatic SIADH from SCLC, chemotherapy reduces tumor secretion of ADH; hyponatremia typically resolves within weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ADH would worsen SIADH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pituitary isn't the source of ADH here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Surgery is usually not feasible for extensive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium intake alone does not correct SIADH.

questions.topicName: Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A patient with SCLC is noted to have poor tumor apoptosis despite DNA damage. Overexpression of which anti-apoptotic protein most likely contributes to tumor cell survival?

explanation.summary: BCL2 overexpression suppresses apoptosis in SCLC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some SCLCs overexpress BCL2, inhibiting mitochondrial apoptosis pathway and promoting cell survival.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BAX is pro-apoptotic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Caspase-3 is an effector of apoptosis, not anti-apoptotic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: p53 promotes apoptosis (and is often mutated/lost in SCLC).
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fas ligand induces apoptosis.

questions.topicName: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with chronic cough, hemoptysis, and a 5-lb weight loss. Labs reveal a serum calcium of 12.8 mg/dL. Chest x-ray shows a central hilar mass. Which NSCLC subtype is most consistent with these findings?

explanation.summary: Central location plus hypercalcemia strongly suggests squamous cell carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Squamous cell carcinoma typically arises centrally in bronchial airways and is the NSCLC subtype most associated with hypercalcemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenocarcinoma is peripheral, not typically hypercalcemic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Large cell carcinoma is peripheral and less common.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Small cell is not NSCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bronchoalveolar is the old name for adenocarcinoma in situ, which is peripheral.

questions.topicName: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (Advanced)
questions.stem: A 42-year-old never-smoker woman is diagnosed with a peripheral lung adenocarcinoma. Molecular testing shows an EGFR exon 19 deletion. Which targeted therapy is most appropriate to initiate?

explanation.summary: EGFR-mutant NSCLC responds to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as osimertinib.
explanation.whyCorrect: Osimertinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting EGFR and is indicated for EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
